concept.name: Borrow-cost model
concept.definition: A model of fees and constraints incurred when maintaining short positions in borrowed securities.
concept.intuition: It is part of the machinery that converts strategy instructions into simulated positions, cash flows, and performance.
concept.mechanics: For each short position, apply the dated borrow rate and availability to market value over elapsed time, accrue the charge, and reject or recall unavailable borrow when modeled.
concept.failure_modes: Simplified timing, liquidity, fee, borrow, funding, or corporate-action assumptions can make simulated results unattainable live.
concept.misconceptions: A detailed simulator reduces modeling error but cannot reproduce every queue event or future market condition.
concept.example: Borrowing $100,000 of stock for 30 days at 6% annualized accrues about $493 on an actual/365 basis.

citations.source: CFA Institute Research Foundation, Investment Model Validation
